body:
Storm Smart: 1. Go inside a building right away. 2. Until the storm is over. 3. Studies the sky and tells us what weather is coming. 4. Drawing shows a building (a house or school) with the student inside.
Safe Inside: the drawing shows the student inside a building (a home, school or store), away from the storm, and the student tells that they go inside and stay there until the storm is over. Under a tree or on the playground is Not yet.
Weather Reporter: answers depend on the day. A full report names the weather, clothes that fit it, and a matching tip (for example, sunny and hot: wear a hat, drink water; rainy: wear boots; cold: wear mittens; thunder: stay inside).
Weather Safety Check: 1. Go inside a building and stay there until the storm is over. 2. Drink water, rest in the shade or wear a sun hat. 3. Hands, ears and head (mittens, a hat, a coat). 4. Studies the sky and tells us what weather is coming. 5. Drawing shows a safe choice that matches the weather.
Scoring tip: "hide under a tree" in a thunderstorm is not safe; score it Not yet and reteach. A student who names a safe place but not what to do there is Getting there on "I can tell what to do in a storm".
title: Answer key: Stay Safe in Any Weather
